subject: ring-tailed lemur
title: Male Lemurs Fight by Waving Stink at Each Other With Their Tails

scenes.text: These animals fight by smelling bad at each other.
Male ring-tailed lemurs have scent glands on wrists and chest: one makes clear liquid, the other a foul brown paste.
Before a fight, a male mixes the two and smears the blend on his tail.
Then rivals face off, tails arched overhead, flicking stink at each other until one retreats.
The scent holds more than 200 chemicals, and it changes with his health.
So lemurs can smell weakness. An injured male's scent loses a tenth of its ingredients, and rivals get more aggressive.

description:
Male ring-tailed lemurs fight by waving their own stink at each other.
Each male has a gland on the inside of the wrist that makes a clear liquid and one on the chest that makes a foul brown paste. He rubs the two together, smears the blend on his tail, then arches the tail over his back and flicks the scent at a rival until one of them retreats. Research at the Duke Lemur Center led by Christine Drea found the scent contains 200 to 300 compounds and carries information about who a lemur is and what condition he is in. When a lemur is wounded, the number of compounds drops by about 10 percent, and males respond more aggressively to a scent that smells off. Males also use a spur on each wrist to gouge tree trunks before marking them.
